html:
A Maya book of astronomy and ritual, made around the 11th or 12th century, probably in the region of Chichén Itzá in Yucatán. It is one of only four Maya books that survive. The rest were lost to time or burned by Spanish priests.

It is painted on bark paper folded like a screen, 39 leaves long. Its pages use Maya writing and the Maya calendar to give:

  • tables that predict eclipses of the sun and moon
  • tables that follow the cycles of the planet Venus, which mattered for timing war and ritual
  • almanacs for divination, and rites for the new year

The codex went to Europe in the 1500s and was bought for the royal library at Dresden in 1739, which gave it its name. Its Venus and eclipse tables helped scholars of the late 1800s first crack Maya numbers and dates. It was damaged by water during the bombing of Dresden in 1945.
